Main.sentence: State Elementary School Menteng 01 ( ___E:Indonesian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_language)___ : Sekolah Dasar Negeri Menteng 01 ), also known as SDN Besuki or the Besuki school , is an ___E:Indonesian public school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education_in_Indonesia)___ in ___E:Menteng U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menteng)___ , ___E:Jakarta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakarta)___ .

Former United States President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ attended the school for one and a half years when he was ___E:growing up in Indonesia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_life_and_career_of_Barack_Obama)___ .

The school was founded in 1934 as Carpentier Alting Stichting Nassau School (CAS)  by the ___E:Dutch colonial administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_East_Indies)___ and was reserved for Dutch children and children of the Indonesian nobility.
The Indonesian government took over administration of the school in 1962, and has since been run by the Raden Saleh Foundation.

Notable former students include the children of Bambang Trihatmodjo, son of former president ___E:Suharto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suharto)___ , the grandchildren of former vice presidents ___E:Hamzah Haz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamzah_Haz)___ and ___E:Try Sutrisno U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Try_Sutrisno)___ , as well as the Dutch author ___E:Tonke Dragt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonke_Dragt)___ .

In 1970–71, ___E:US President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ attended the school for one and a half years.

Obama's announcement of his candidacy for United States president in January, 2007 drew worldwide media attention to the school, with many media outlets sending reporters there, including The Chicago Tribune ,   ___E:NBC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC)___ ,  and the ___E:BBC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC)___ .  ___E:Nedra Pickler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nedra_Pickler)___ of the ___E:Associated Press U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press)___ reported: "Those tied to the school say they are proud to have had a student like Obama, and hope that, if he is elected president, his ties to Indonesia will broaden his world perspective and his views on religion."
In 2010, a statue of Barack Obama as a child was installed at the school.
